correctness.rationale: Mirabi’s tree-closure requires each present parent to include each singleton-labeled child and all ancestors. Each infinity-child color contributes a finite multiset of rooted types; inductive classification gives the exact Euler transform. When infinity colors form an antichain, every branch is a rigid forced-size copy, yielding a restricted-partition Euler product, quasipolynomial coefficients, and a lattice-simplex leading constant. Comparable infinity colors yield independently chosen branches with pairwise distinct sizes b+cj, giving 2^k distinct types of size O(k^2). The series converges absolutely for |z|<1 by induction on finite plan height, giving subexponential cumulative growth. The real verifier independently confirms 42474 finite assertions and the structural arguments establish the unlimited result.

originality.rationale: The existing finite-tree-plan model theory constructs and counts vertices of the uniform approximants, but not color-preserving isomorphism types of arbitrary finite tree-closed subtrees by their closure size. Polynomial oligomorphic group profile theory counts subset orbits, which is a distinct grading. The restricted partition and Euler transform ingredients are known; the specific plan-controlled all-case dichotomy, rational subclass formula, sharp degree, and nested intermediate growth were not located in the inspected sources. Unindexed folklore or a stronger implicit species-theoretic result remains possible.

value.rationale: Provides a motivated natural exact invariant (color-preserving finite tree-closure hull types) for a published family of countable tree models. It gives a recursion for every finite plan, a structural yes/no growth criterion based only on plan infinity-node comparability, exact sharp polynomial degree and leading constant in the polynomial regime, and an all-height superpolynomial/subexponential contrast in the nested regime. The canonical depth-two case connects these closures to partition growth while |Γ(m)| remains polynomial. This is more than recomputing a classical partition table.
